Its missing-additive-inverses warning concerns semiring-module direct sums, not the disjoint assignment of deterministic execution rounds to a largest misplaced value.
Its failure is a ray-orientation ambiguity hidden by slopes and arctangent; this draft uses only discrete list order and integer comparisons.
Its missing-additive-cancellation warning applies to leading coefficients over polynomial semirings, while the retained identities partition and telescope ordinary integer move counts.
It refutes a KL-divergence identification in a Chernoff exponent; no probability distribution, entropy, logarithm, or analogous analytic identity is used here.
Its missing consistency hypothesis concerns monotone f-values in A* search; the target algorithm has no heuristic or best-first expansion.
Its chess branching count fails because promotions change legal moves and piece multiplicities; the target always retains one copy of each fixed permutation value.
Its defect is an off-by-one geometric-tree ancestor count for a stone-pile move graph; no branching-tree volume estimate or geometric sum appears in the retained Θ(n+M) proof.
Its counterexample concerns unjustified uniqueness of a maximum clique; no maximum clique or analogous extremizer is asserted unique in this draft.
It is a false real inequality involving a square root and an epsilon-N argument; no such inequality appears in any retained bound or checker.

It concerns a subtraction-by-one recursion that fails a quotient specification; there is no division recursion or quotient claim in this draft.

results.claim: The literal optimized algorithm’s complexity is Θ(n+M), where M=Σ_t d(p_t) along its actual FIFO trajectory, but the ordered queue is part of the state.
results.proof_sketch: Let p_t be the shelf and q_t=(x_1,…,x_k) the current FIFO queue. Initialization puts the left-to-right descent bottoms in q_0. A local adjacency induction using the pseudocode’s two enqueue tests shows that, at every round boundary, q_t contains exactly the descent bottoms D(p_t) as a set, although not necessarily in shelf order. Processing q_t yields p_{t+1}=reverse(q_t) followed by the elements outside q_t in their previous relative order. Hence |q_t|=d(p_t) and M is the total number of queue pops. The initial scan costs Θ(n), and every pop performs Θ(1) pointer and queue work. The queue’s order is history-dependent, so p_{t+1}=reverse(D(p_t)) followed by U(p_t) is not a valid autonomous transition.

results.claim: There is an exact phase decomposition that isolates the unresolved cost.
results.proof_sketch: Let i be the largest unfixed value and let s_i<i be its position when its phase begins. Every larger value belongs to a permanent fixed suffix, so i is never marked. In a round, moving an element that began left of i shifts i left on removal and right on prepending, for net zero. Moving one that began right of i shifts i right exactly once. If q_t and ℓ_t count the moved elements respectively right and left of i, then i advances by q_t. Consequently Σ_t q_t=i−s_i over the phase, and its exact move cost is (i−s_i)+Σ_tℓ_t. This is independent of the FIFO processing order.

results.claim: The parent’s Ω(n^{3/2}) lower bound and coefficient (4√2/3+o(1)) are not established for the literal optimized FIFO algorithm.
results.proof_sketch: The staircase recurrence describes the ordinary shelf-ordered transition, not the persistent FIFO queue. For P_6=(6,1,2,3,4,5), after three rounds the ordinary transition has state (3,1,2,6,4,5), whereas the literal optimized pseudocode has (1,3,2,6,4,5). Thus the claimed prefix identity already fails at this finite boundary, and its subsequent summation cannot supply a lower bound for the target algorithm.

results.claim: For n≤9, the exact maximum numbers of moves are 0,1,3,6,11,18,27,38,53.
results.proof_sketch: All 409,113 permutations of sizes 1 through 9 were exhaustively executed under the literal FIFO pseudocode. Three implementations—vector-based, std::list-based, and a value-indexed predecessor/successor array—agreed on every queue, boundary state, round count, and move total. The maxima were attained and no enumerated permutation exceeded them.

results.claim: A natural twice-per-unordered-pair charging bound is false.
results.proof_sketch: For p=(2,4,…,4096,1,3,…,4095), exact literal-FIFO execution makes 49,545,006 moves. This exceeds 2·binom(4096,2)=16,773,120, so a charging argument allowing at most two moves for each unordered pair cannot cover every execution. This is only a finite obstruction to that charging rule; it does not itself refute an O(n²) asymptotic bound.

results.claim: No asymptotically tight worst-case bound is proved here; the authorized Ω(n log n)–O(n³) interval remains unresolved.
results.proof_sketch: The only parent claim that purported to improve the asymptotic lower bound uses the invalid shelf-ordered transition. The surviving phase identity isolates an uncontrolled left-of-active term, while the corrected finite maxima and pair-charging witness provide no infinite-family estimate. Therefore neither endpoint of the authorized interval is improved in this revision.

final_writeup:
Resolution status: PARTIAL. The requested asymptotically tight worst-case complexity remains open; this revision does not improve the authorized Ω(n log n)–O(n³) interval.

The essential correction is that the literal optimized pseudocode has an extended state. At the start of round t, let p_t be the shelf and q_t the ordered FIFO queue. The set of entries of q_t is the set D(p_t) of descent bottoms, but its order may differ from their current left-to-right shelf order. If q_t=(x_1,…,x_k), processing it gives

p_{t+1}=reverse(q_t)·U(p_t),

where U(p_t) deletes the elements in q_t while preserving all other relative order. Meanwhile the two local tests in the pseudocode construct q_{t+1}. Thus the optimized running time is Θ(n+M), with M=Σ_t|q_t|=Σ_t d(p_t), but the trajectory cannot be generated from p_t alone by the parent’s transition reverse(D(p_t))·U(p_t).

The smallest audited distinction used here is p=(4,1,5,2,6,3). Its first boundary is (3,2,1,4,5,6) with optimized queue (1,2), although the shelf-order descent sequence is (2,1). The optimized process therefore reaches (2,1,3,4,5,6), then sorts in a third round, for 6 moves total. The parent transition sorts in two rounds with 5 moves. Likewise, for P_6 the two processes already disagree after round three. This invalidates the claimed staircase transfer and removes both the Ω(n^{3/2}) assertion and its coefficient.

The verified phase decomposition survives because it does not depend on queue order. During the phase of the largest unfixed value i, every moved element initially to its right advances i once, while every moved element initially to its left has zero net effect on i. If the phase begins at position s_i, the right-side moves sum exactly to i−s_i, and the phase cost is

(i−s_i) + (number of moves made left of i during the phase).

Controlling the second term remains the structural obstacle.

Exact enumeration under the literal pseudocode corrects the finite maxima for n=1,…,9 to 0,1,3,6,11,18,27,38,53. The parent’s P_13 count also changes from 161 to 97 moves. The twice-per-unordered-pair claim remains correct with a repaired witness: the even-then-odd permutation of size 4096 makes 49,545,006 moves, exceeding 16,773,120. That finite inequality rules out the stated charging scheme but proves no asymptotic lower bound.

Accordingly, the phase identity and corrected computations are valid structural progress and constitute material partial progress under the audit taxonomy, but they do not solve the target’s asymptotic question. claimed_resolution is therefore PARTIAL, directly addressing the audit’s target-coverage and understated-resolution judgments.
